side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "A proposal seats at most once. A widening that cites an acceptance an admitted widening has already consumed is not admissible, so one invitation never admits twice."

note: A builder of 'a proposal seats at most once' spends the standing proposal on the first joiner, so an open room admits one person per proposal; a builder of CC 3.2 admits every requester. Admission rule (5) ('P has not already seated K'), CC 3.2 and the CC 8.10 guard (spent per acceptance) support the per-joiner reading; the 'seats at most once' sentence needs the standing offer excepted.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "an acceptance or decline is the invitee's only — the signer resolves (`signer_acts_for`, [CC 3.4.7.3](part_3_the_namespace.md)) to the proposal's `subject_key_ids[0]`"

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1 A relay forwards the canonical octets as received. A relay that re-serializes from a parsed object at all MUST emit JCS
side_b: CC 2.6.1.3 requires it to re-canonicalize member order while holding member presence/absence fixed. So what it forwards is the canonical form
note: 2.6.1.1 and 2.6.1.5 forward the received octets and re-order only on re-serialising; 2.6.1.3 says 2.6.1.1 requires re-canonicalising, so a pretty-printed arrival is forwarded as received by one reader and as JCS by the other. Signatures verify either way; a downstream intake ceiling may refuse the first.

side_a: CC 2.6.6 15-character lowercase hex string (no `0x` prefix; per [CC 2.6.3](#2.6.3))
side_b: CC 2.6.3 **byte-length-exact** (a SHA-256 digest is exactly 64 hex characters)
note: A 64-bit H3 index is 16 hex characters byte-exact; the 15-character form drops the leading zero nibble while 2.6.6 also says leading zeros are preserved. Every example in the text (8001fffffffffff, 85283473fffffff) has 15, so 15 is what the document supports.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 no `0x`, no separators, byte-length-exact; never base64 in canonical bytes
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2 The member carries both halves raw, in the standard base64 of
note: 2.6.1.1.1 puts public keys under the hex rule and says never base64 in canonical bytes; onion_hop_pubkeys (3.3.6.2) and encryption_pubkeys (4.4.3.4.3.1) are public keys inside the signed bytes as base64. The "explicitly documented as base64" clause covers them but names only an opaque blob as its example; the member names (_base64) settle it.

side_a: CC 3.1.2.1 lexicographically by byte representation BEFORE canonicalization
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)
note: 3.1.2.1 sorts capability_declaration by bytes and then says all 2.6.1.1.1 rules apply, whose set order is UTF-16 code units. The two orders differ only for strings with characters above U+FFFF against U+E000 to U+FFFF; capability strings are ASCII in practice.

side_a: CC 6.1.1 **Leaf order MUST be lexicographic** over leaf bytes (the [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) set-semantics rule)
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)
note: 6.1.1 cites the 2.6.1.1.1 set rule as its leaf order, but that rule is UTF-16 code-unit order and 6.1.1, 6.1.2.1.2 and 6.1.5.2 sort raw (UTF-8) bytes. Same result for ASCII ids; the Part 6 statements agree with each other on raw bytes.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 Parsers MUST tolerate the trailing `:vN` version segment.
side_b: CC 3.1.7 A dimension without it is refused with **`missing_version_segment`**

side_a: CC 3.3.2 HPKE RFC 9180 base-mode shape; X25519 KEM + HKDF-SHA-256 KDF + AES-256-GCM AEAD. **v1**.
side_b: CC 3.3.2 The wrap is `wrap_algorithm` (v2 only) and `wrapped_dek`.
note: Still present (held: a Part 3 table row). The table keeps the v1 wire string as a known value, so fail-secure decode does not refuse it; "v2 only" and CC 5.1 ("never v1") refuse it, and 5.1 states the consumer refusal only for a streaming epoch grant. A v1 content-axis wrap is admitted by one reader and refused by the other.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per RNS Link (transit replay guard).
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is a per-`(link, stream)` counter both ends keep and is never carried in the frame
note: Still present (to fix from the text). One counter per link against one per link and stream: two ends that count differently derive different outer nonces and no frame opens; the nonce formula has no stream id, which supports per link.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature by the bound chunk key, appended to the inner unit after the inner ciphertext and inside the outer seal
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 the shipping form, which precedes the signature with an 8-byte publisher timestamp `source_ms` under the domain `ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v2`
note: Still present (to fix from the text). The laid-out trailer (64 bytes, domain v1, budget 148) and the known answers are of a form the same sentence says no release carries; a relay taking the last 64 bytes under v1 refuses every shipping chunk.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.1 The enforced invariant is therefore only within a single epoch: counter strictly monotonic, never wraps (guaranteed by the forced roll). Across epochs, reset is free.
side_b: CC 5.3.3.1 Substrate MUST reject a chunk-append whose `(stream_id, seq)` collides with an existing sealed chunk (the replay and forking guard).
note: Still open. 5.3.3.2.5 makes the counter the header chunk_seq; if it resets each epoch the (stream_id, seq) guard refuses the second epoch and the 5.3.3.3 leaf order by seq is not a total order; if it does not reset, a stream ends near 2^32 chunks.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 Every `accord:invoke:*` Contribution signs the canonical bytes below.
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 The signing input is JCS(`attestation_envelope`) ([CC 2.6.1.3](#2.6.1.3)) and nothing else
note: Still present (to fix from the text). 4.2.1.1, 4.2.1.3 and 4.2.6 each lay out a labelled newline-joined preimage for a row and name no member that carries a second signature; a verifier of the halt row checks one preimage or the other.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 id = sha256(domain ‖ JCS(object)); a receiver re-derives the row and refuses any byte difference
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 minted by the stamper before the bytes exist (a UUID; this edition pins no version)
note: Still present (to fix from the text). The carrier row id is a 32-byte digest in 3.1.3 and a 36-character uuid in the table and the CDDL, with no fold stated; receivers that re-derive with different folds refuse each other's row.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.6 A phantom / self-invented root → REJECT.
side_b: CC 8.10 one transparency_log:inclusion@admitted[val:root_hash=val:chunk_root] else advise
note: Still present in manifests/transitions.json and the card (also C510). The text refuses a receipt over an unpublished root (step 2, MUST) and only recommends the inclusion proof (step 3); the data types step 3 as advisory and has nothing for step 2, so the data admits a receipt the text refuses.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 32 bytes (caller-derived: sha256(stream_meta))
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 which MUST equal `SHA-256("ciris-edge:call-stream:v2" ‖ room ‖ publisher ‖ join_nonce)` with no length prefixes
note: The layout line gives the stream id as a digest of an undefined stream_meta; the binding rule in the same section pins it and refuses any other (av_binding_stream_not_derived). The MUST with its token governs; the layout comment is the loose side.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.1 the codec itself is named by the stream's binding, never by this id, which carries layer semantics only
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 Its encoding is a fixed big-endian concatenation, no CBOR and no JSON: `version` (u8, `0x01`); `room` and `publisher`
note: The StreamKeyBinding has seven fixed members and none names a codec; the only stated home of a stream-level codec is the `codec` stream field of 3.3.13. A receiver of codec_id 0x04 cannot learn H.264 from VP8 out of the binding.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 collision-safety rides the [CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2) single-sender-per-`(stream_id, epoch)` invariant
side_b: CC 5.3.3.1 **Single-sender-per-`(stream_id, epoch)` invariant (normative — nonce-collision safety; as in SFrame/MLS)**
note: Citation: the invariant is stated in 5.3.3.1, not 5.3.3.2.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.8 every other signed thing except the chunk trailer becomes a COSE object with its own `typ`, so no hand-laid layout and no little-endian field remains
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 Its encoding is a fixed big-endian concatenation, no CBOR and no JSON
note: 2.6.1.8 (planned edition) keeps only the chunk trailer hand-laid. The stream key binding, the receipt and stream-root layouts (5.3.3.6, 5.3.3.3), the accord preimages and the 6.1.3 binary preimages are stated without an edition, and 6.1.3 forbids any other encoding; none says it ends with the new edition.

side_a: CC 6.1.1 a wholeness witness is a federation-tier attestation: hybrid PQC verified at ingest
side_b: CC 6.1.3 **transport/substrate framing**: binary, never a CC 2.1 Contribution, never an `attestation_type`
note: 6.1.1 calls the witness an attestation under a namespace `wholeness_witness:`; 6.1.3 says every Part 6 preimage but the census rows is binary framing and never an attestation. No such family is registered and no preimage is laid out; 6.1.3 and 3.4.10 (a node's own state-root commitment) agree on framing.

side_a: CC 3.2 Its **digest** is the SHA-256 of the record's signed bytes (its row hash).
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 Store-computed over the row's own serialisation (not JCS), excluding itself
note: Row hash is the table's name for persist_row_hash, which is not over the signed bytes and is not a conformance target; the digest 3.2 defines is the SHA-256 of the signing input (original_content_hash). 5.3.1 ("named by the SHA-256 of its signed bytes") supports the latter.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 `evidence_refs[]` stays bare sha256.
side_b: CC 3.3.13 sha256:<hex>   over the bytes as stored and forwarded; == evidence_refs[]
note: One line says the entry is a bare SHA-256, the field set says it equals the `sha256:`-prefixed digest, and 5.3.2.5 and 3.3.2 also admit a URI. The vectors (manifests/signed_object_vectors.json) carry `sha256:<hex>` and a URL, so "bare" reads as "no CID wrapper"; the exact spelling is pinned nowhere in prose.

side_a: CC 2.6.2 Every ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 datetime in this specification MUST be:

note: The columns beside the row (asserted_at, expires_at, scrub_timestamp, pqc_completed_at, key record valid_from and valid_until) are typed as any string, and scrub_timestamp has no signed twin. A reader of 2.6.2 refuses a column not in the millisecond Z form; a reader of the table compares instants. The mirror check (typed_diverges_from_envelope) does not say which.

note: The schema admits any lowercase algorithm label and any hex length (canonical:md5:ab passes); the text refuses all but sha256 with 64 characters. The schema is looser than the gate; the text governs.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3.1 signed_at: <rfc3339_canonical> }
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 When the signature was issued: asserted_at, or widened_at on a widening. Outside the bytes.
note: Beside C438 (flat member set against the row mirror). Member sets (b) and (c) put a `signed_at` inside the signed bytes, and (b) lists no asserted_at; the table has no signed_at member, requires asserted_at inside, and keeps the signing instant outside as scrub_timestamp.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 "nonce=" || base64url(rand_32_bytes) || "\n" ||
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 every field documented as base64 MUST use the RFC 4648 §4 STANDARD alphabet, WITH padding, no whitespace or embedded newlines
note: The accord preimages (4.2.1.1, 4.2.1.3, 4.2.6) encode the nonce base64url, padding unstated, against the one pinned base64 variant. A verifier that re-encodes the nonce bytes instead of using the carried string gets other bytes.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.4 **advertised over the existing `federation_session` / `key_grant` entitlement surface — NOT a new wire**

note: The receiver's layer cap is said to ride the key_grant surface, but an unkept call has no key_grant row and the 3.3.2 member list has no policy member; 5.3.3.2.1 and 5.3.3.4 have the receiver ask per layer on the link. Where the cap is carried is stated two ways.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.1 `destination_hash = hash(x25519 ‖ ed25519)`
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2.1 it is **NOT** a single SHA-256 over a flat `x25519 ‖ ed25519 ‖ app_name ‖ aspects` preimage
note: 3.3.6.1 (and the lead of 3.3.6.2) write the destination as a hash of the two keys; the pinned algorithm is two-stage, over a name hash and an identity hash, truncated to 16 bytes. The pinned section governs and says so; the shorthand is the loose side.

side_a: CC 3.1.5 "sha256:"-prefixed, hex per CC 2.6.3
side_b: CC 2.6.3 **unpadded** (no leading `0x`, no separators), and **byte-length-exact**
note: Some digest members carry a `sha256:` prefix (trace_manifest content_hash, the Source struct digest, bundle_fingerprint) and others are bare 64-hex (content_sha256, at_rest_sha256, original_content_hash). 2.6.1.1.1 exempts only the canonical: tag from the no-separators rule; no rule says which digest members are prefixed.

side_b: CC 4.2.6: "The proposal and the participation each sign a distinct, wire-isolated canonical-bytes domain"
note: Text against text. CC 3.2 and the CC 3.1.3 group:roster row make an accord roster version a cosigned row: additional_scrubs over the record's own canonical bytes, reaching the roster-change threshold. CC 4.2.6 has each holder sign an accord_participation preimage (a vote over the proposer's nonce) and says the decision bundle signs nothing. A verifier built from one refuses the roster change the other produces; no sentence says how participations become the version's cosignatures. side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: "group=affiliations & seats=one => affiliation_member_action@subject_group"
note: Text against data. The affiliation_member_action arm exists on membership:{stage} (leaf removal) and nowhere else. quarantine:{state} and slashing:{outcome} have count none and a one-signer attest; takedown_notice:{basis} has a cosigned case for steward_purge only. A kernel run from the data lets the one deciding seat of an affiliation quarantine, slash or take down a member's content alone, where the text leaves such an act a proposal.
